function: Excluded (function): the DRL learns UAV trajectories, user associations and channel selections for UAV-assisted MEC under jamming, an anti-jamming MEC task outside the seven areas (pp. 1, 3, 8).
notes: Exclusion function (anti-jamming). The above_phy check passes under the aerial-link rule: the policy learns trajectory and user association (above PHY) jointly with channel selection, which the paper presents as spectrum allocation on the UAV links (p. 4: "the channels for each UAV to receive image tasks need to be selected to allocate spectrum resources reasonably"). The learned actions on p. 8 are the UAV moving distance and direction, the association with a text user and with a vehicle, and the channel selection (p. 8: "each agent will decide its trajectory and user association"); transmit power and beams are not actions, and no antenna array, MIMO or RIS is modeled. The task is anti-jamming UAV-assisted MEC: p. 3: "combines multi-modal semantic communication with anti-jamming strategies"; antijamming is an index term (p. 1); the objective on p. 7 is delay and semantic accuracy: "to maximum the semantic accuracy and minimize total communication and computation delay". The semantic codec DeepSC-VQA is pre-trained and only supplies the semantic rate (p. 5: "the results after encoding and decoding can be directly used"; p. 6: "For the pre-trained DeepSC-VQA model"), so semantic coding is not a learned function here. Results are reward, delay and semantic accuracy against SC-D4N, SC-MA-DDPG, SC-MA-TD3-F and N-SC-MA-TD3 (pp. 11-14). REVIEWER CHECK: if channel selection is read as a non-physical-layer decision, the code would be above_phy instead of function; if it is read as area-6 resource control of an aerial link, the work would need full grading as area 6. A complexity order is given on pp. 10-11; no code or data link is given.
